content: When nitroglycerin is administered sublingually, it may cause a burning or tingling sensation. However, the presence or absence of this sensation should not be used as a reliable indicator of the potency of the tablets. Headaches are a potential side effect of nitroglycerin treatment. In patients who experience these headaches, the occurrence of the headache may serve as an indicator of the drug's pharmacological activity. Nitroglycerin treatment can lead to lightheadedness, particularly when standing up, especially after transitioning from a recumbent or seated position. This effect is more likely to occur in individuals who have consumed alcohol. Nitroglycerin tablets should always be stored in their original glass container and must be tightly capped after each use to prevent a loss of potency. The use of nitroglycerin in conjunction with alcohol can increase the likelihood of experiencing lightheadedness upon standing, particularly after rising from a seated or lying position. This effect is more pronounced in patients who have consumed alcohol. The simultaneous use of nitrates and alcohol may result in hypotension, which is a significant drop in blood pressure.
